help.title: Help
help.swagger_description: Swagger UI - Interactive REST API explorer
help.open_tor: Open Tor Browser and wait for it to connect
help.paste_onion: Copy the onion address above and paste it into Tor Browser's address bar
help.rest_intro: The REST API is the primary interface: every feature of the web UI is available through it. All endpoints live under {endpoint}, answer application/json by default and wrap results as {ok_example} (errors: {error_example}). Add .txt or send Accept: text/plain for plain text.
help.graphql_endpoint: The GraphQL endpoint is {graphql}; the OpenAPI spec is served at {swagger}.
help.web_create_title: Create a paste via the web
help.web_create_body: Go to /create, fill in your content, choose a language and expiry, then click Create Paste. Save the delete token — it is shown only once.
help.burn_body: Set burn_after to a number 1–9999. The paste is deleted after that many views. Set to 0 to disable.
help.compat_intro: Compatibility endpoints are separate from the native API above. They reproduce the wire protocol of other paste services so existing scripts and CLIs work unmodified. Compat creates are anonymous (any API key is accepted and ignored) and use each service's own delete convention, not the owner token.
help.compat_dropin: This server is a drop-in replacement for multiple paste services. Point existing scripts and CLIs here without modification:
help.wire_compat: Wire-compatible with the {name} API:
help.sk_row_create: Create paste (form text/title/name/lang/expire/private; apikey accepted and ignored); returns the view URL {view_url} as plain text, or Error: <msg>
help.sk_row_view: Redirects to the native paste view
help.hb_row_create: Create paste from the raw request body; returns {key_example}
help.hb_row_get: Get paste content as {data_example} ({missing_example} if missing)
help.dp_row_create: Create paste; format=url returns bare URL, format=json returns JSON
help.curlupload_intro: Wire-compatible with the curl-upload one-liner family:
help.curlupload_row: Upload via multipart file (0x0.st), form sprunge (sprunge.us), or form f:1 (ix.io); returns a bare raw-content URL {raw_url}. Requests with none of these fields fall through to the native paste-create handler.
help.curlupload_token: The 0x0.st style also returns an X-Token response header — the paste's compat delete token, mirroring the 0x0.st management-token convention.
help.termbin_intro: Wire-compatible with termbin.com and the fiche server protocol. Connect, stream content, close the write side; the server replies with the paste URL and closes:
help.termbin_limits: Maximum payload: {size} bytes. Idle/read timeout: {timeout}. TCP port: {port}.
help.subdomain_intro: Any target can also be reached by using its label as the leftmost part of the hostname (for example hb. before this server's hostname). On a matched subdomain, a bare POST / with a raw body creates a paste for that target, and other targets' routes are hidden.
help.tor_intro: This service is available as a Tor hidden service for enhanced privacy.
help.tor_step_paste: Paste the onion address above into the Tor Browser address bar
help.tor_privacy_note: Using Tor hides your IP address and encrypts your connection through the Tor network.
help.i2p_intro: This service is available as an I2P eepsite for enhanced privacy.
help.i2p_step_install: Install I2P or i2pd and wait for it to integrate with the network
help.i2p_step_proxy: Configure your browser to use the I2P HTTP proxy (default 127.0.0.1:4444)
help.i2p_step_paste: Copy the .b32.i2p address above and paste it into your browser address bar
help.i2p_note: Using I2P routes your connection through the I2P network. Eepsites are served over http:// — the I2P tunnel provides the transport encryption, so no TLS certificate is used.
help.faq_q_account: Do I need an account or API key?
help.faq_a_account: No. Creating, reading, and deleting pastes requires no authentication. The delete token returned at creation is all you need to remove a paste.
help.faq_a_retention: Until their expiry elapses (see the expiry table above) or their burn-after view count is reached. Pastes set to never are kept until deleted.
help.faq_a_size: Yes. The server enforces a maximum paste size of {size}; oversized content is rejected with a 413 response.
help.faq_q_scripts: Can I use it from scripts?
help.faq_a_scripts: Yes — pipe to curl --data-binary @-, use the JSON API, or point existing pastebin.com scripts at this server.
help.ts_404_body: The paste ID is wrong or the paste has expired or been burned. Check the URL.
help.ts_413_body: Your content exceeds the maximum paste size. Split it or reduce the size.
help.ts_429_body: You have hit the rate limit. Wait and retry; the Retry-After header tells you how long.
help.ts_403_body: The delete token is missing or incorrect. Only the correct token can delete a paste.

security.title: Security
security.meta_description: How to report a security vulnerability in {site} — contact channels, disclosure policy, and encryption key
security.how_to_report_text: If you believe you have found a security vulnerability, please report it privately through one of the channels below, in order of preference. Do not open a public issue or disclose the details until we have had a chance to investigate and coordinate a fix.
security.channel_form_text: Following this link opens the security-report form; the report body is encrypted at rest and never stored in plaintext.
security.encryption_text: For sensitive details, encrypt your report with our PGP public key, available at:
security.link_policy_desc: scope, safe harbor, and coordinated-disclosure window
security.link_txt_desc: the machine-readable version of this page (RFC 9116)
security.policy_meta_description: Coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy for {site} — scope, safe harbor, and how to report
security.reporting_text: We welcome reports from security researchers. Reports are submitted through a rotating, single-use link published in our security.txt file. Following that link opens an encrypted reporting form; the report body is encrypted at rest and is never stored in plaintext.
security.pgp_available: Our PGP public key for encrypting sensitive details is available at:
security.disclosure_window_text: We ask that you give us up to {days} days to investigate and remediate a reported issue before any public disclosure, or until a coordinated disclosure date is mutually agreed — whichever comes first. We will keep you updated through your report's status page.
security.in_scope_1: This service and its official domains
security.in_scope_3: The public REST, GraphQL, and web endpoints
security.out_scope_1: Denial-of-service, volumetric, or rate-limit exhaustion testing
security.out_scope_2: Social engineering, phishing, or physical attacks against staff
security.out_scope_3: Automated scanner output without a demonstrated, reproducible impact
security.out_scope_4: Reports affecting only unsupported or end-of-life versions
security.out_scope_5: Attacks requiring a compromised host, rooted device, or physical access
security.safe_harbor_text: We will not pursue or support legal action against researchers who act in good faith, respect this policy, avoid privacy violations and data destruction, and give us reasonable time to respond before disclosing. Testing must stay within the scope above, use your own test data, and stop at the first sign of access to another user's data. Activity conducted consistently with this policy is considered authorized.
security.acknowledgments_text: With your permission, we credit researchers who report valid issues on our acknowledgments page.
security.status_rate_limited: This status link may only be opened once per day. You are seeing the last loaded state; please check back tomorrow for a fresh view.
security.status_contact_text: To add information to this report, reply to the acknowledgment email and include your tracking ID.
security.thanks_subtitle: Thank you to the researchers who help keep {site} safe
security.thanks_meta_description: Researchers we thank for responsibly disclosing security issues in {site}
security.thanks_intro: We are grateful to the following researchers for responsibly disclosing security issues under our security policy.
security.thanks_empty: No disclosures have been published yet. If you have found a security issue, please review our security policy and report it responsibly.
